title: TPRL: Adaptive Visual Token Pruning in LVLMs via Language-Guided Reinforcement Learning
claim: A costly multi-step selection process is learned in three staged phases: compress state, imitate demonstrations, then refine with reinforcement learning.
layout: 3 panels: two small top, one wide bottom; left-to-right flow, dashed cross-link
description: A wide figure split into three labeled panels. Panel (a), top left on a gray background, shows an autoencoder: grids of fine-grained tokens pass through a trapezoid Encoder into coarser latent tokens, then a Decoder reconstructs them. Panel (b), top right, shows learning from demonstrations. A bird photo is progressively masked with gray grid cells in a pruning-demonstration row. Below it, a training-policy row runs the same photo through an encoder and policy networks, with Loss arrows linking the two rows. Panel (c), the large bottom section, shows RL training with PPO. A butterfly image and the question text feed a vision encoder, projector, encoder and token embedding. These produce yellow visual tokens and green text tokens. The tokens go through repeated policy-network steps (t=1, t=2, t=3), each with a prune marker and reward, critic and advantage boxes, ending at an LLM module. A legend sits at the top left, and a dashed arrow links the encoder in (a) to (c). Pastel yellow, green and blue boxes carry the flow.
caption: Overview of the TPRL framework consisting of three synergistic stages. (a) Autoencoder training for state compression learns a compact latent representation to reduce the feature dimensionality of each visual token. (b) Learning from demonstrations provides a foundational initialization for the pruning policy by imitating high-quality trajectories to ensure stable convergence. (c) RL training using PPO fine-tunes the policy through language-guided sequential optimization to achieve an optimal balance between task performance and computational efficiency.
abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) incur substantial inference costs due to the processing of a vast number of visual tokens. Existing methods typically rely on hand-engineered scoring rules that fail to capture the complex inter-dependencies of progressive visual token reduction, while directly deploying multi-step pruner during inference introduces unacceptable latency. To overcome this dilemma, we propose TPRL, a reinforcement learning framework that leverages sequential multi-step exploration during training to derive a highly adaptive, one-shot pruning policy for efficient inference. During the training phase, we formulate visual token reduction as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) with explicit state transitions, employing a self-supervised autoencoder to compress visual tokens for efficient policy learning. Initialized via learning from demonstrations, the policy is fine-tuned using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to explicitly learn sequential token dependencies and jointly optimize end-task accuracy and computational efficiency. Crucially, at inference time, TPRL deploys this trained policy as a deterministic one-shot selector, amortizing the cost of sequential reasoning into a single forward pass. Our experimental results demonstrate that TPRL removes up to 66.7\% of visual tokens and achieves up to a 65.3\% reduction in FLOPs during inference while maintaining a near-lossless average accuracy drop of only 0.2\% on LLaVA-1.5-7B. Extensive evaluations across diverse architectures further confirm the robust generalizability of our approach.
